explain.say: Here is a sort. I do: walk calmly, stay with my teacher, listen, line up. I leave behind: my bag, lunch box, toys, my work. Aarav did it! So can you. Your challenge: tell a grown-up the fire drill steps.

faq.q: Why is the fire bell so loud?
faq.a: It is loud so every person in the whole building can hear it. You can cover your ears or wear ear defenders if your school says yes.
asks: Tell me about The bell rings

faq.a: No, bags and things stay inside. Leaving them helps everyone get out quickly. They will be there when you come back.
asks: Tell me about I leave behind

faq.q: Why do we have fire drills?
faq.a: A drill is practice. It helps everyone learn what to do, so they stay calm and safe if there is ever a real fire.

faq.q: What if I feel scared in a fire drill?
faq.a: Stay close to your teacher and follow the line. You can hold a friend's hand. A grown-up you trust can tell you before a drill, if they know.

faq.q: Can I know when a drill is coming?
faq.a: Sometimes. You can ask your teacher, Can you tell me before a drill, please? Some schools can do that.

facts: Schools practise fire drills so everyone knows how to leave the building safely.
In a fire drill, people walk, not run, and leave their things behind.
